exemplars.title: Language of Zelda: Facilitating Language Learning Practices Using ChatGPT
exemplars.why: Each NPC dialogue item is immediately rendered in its original form and as an adjacent English translation, cleanly instantiating the pattern’s same-content fan-out across language representations.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: Selected over rid 3456 because its immediately juxtaposed bilingual renderings demonstrate a broader representational form of multimodal output than conventional optional text-to-speech.

exemplars.title: Kya family planning after marriage hoti hai?: Integrating Cultural Sensitivity in an LLM Chatbot for Reproductive Health
exemplars.why: A response remains available as text while a text-to-speech button renders that exact response as audio, matching the structural signature with unusually little ambiguity.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: Selected over rid 6271 because it specifies the user-facing control and exact text-to-audio transformation, making the interaction more directly rebuildable.

exemplars.title: Once Upon AI Time: Combining Narrative and Games for Early AI Literacy
exemplars.why: Full voiceover of all displayed text creates systematic, content-preserving duplication across visual and auditory channels while addressing differences in young children’s reading ability.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: Selected over rid 17071 because “full voiceover of all text” conclusively establishes redundant content, whereas textual, visual, and aural writing suggestions may be complementary or modality-specific.

notes: The final set departs from consensus by moving rid 6271 above rid 17071 and rid 16653. The latter two are more novel, but their excerpts do not establish the pattern’s required redundancy: multimodal writing suggestions could differ by modality, and animation plus narration may divide spatial and verbal information. No score was adjusted by more than 0.3. Readers should distrust any implied outcome claims because the supplied excerpts describe mechanisms rather than measured effects. For rid 8046, the quote conclusively supports bilingual display but is less explicit about audible speech than the rater notes suggest; for rid 6271, games, images, and videos are complementary content and are not themselves evidence of this pattern—the qualifying mechanism is specifically the full voiceover of all text.
